title: Generalizations of Wilsons Theorem to Non-Prime Moduli

problemStatement.formal: For n ≥ 2: (n-1)! ≡ -1 (mod n) iff n prime; (n-1)! ≡ 0 (mod n) for composite n > 4. The Gauss-Wilson classification: ∏ units ≡ -1 (mod n) iff n ∈ {4, p^k, 2p^k}.
problemStatement.plain: Complete classification of factorial residues and unit products modulo n, extending Wilson's theorem to all moduli.
whyMatters: Wilson's theorem is fundamental in number theory
The Gauss generalization connects to primitive root theory

proven: Composite factorial vanishing: n | (n-1)! for composite n > 4
Complete factorial classification for all n ≥ 2
Gauss-Wilson classification verified computationally for n ≤ 300
